PullRequest.Title: chat: clarify merged session cleanup setting descriptions
PullRequest.Body:

Updates only the two merged-session cleanup setting descriptions using the suggested concise wording. Clarifies that marking a session Done follows inactivity and that permanent deletion happens after an additional retention period, with eligible worktrees removed safely.

Setting names/IDs, migrations, defaults, and runtime behavior are unchanged.

Validation:
- `npm run transpile-client` — passed.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessionsConfiguration.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — blocked by a pre-existing Copilot runtime dependency mismatch (declared 1.0.99-0, installed SDK bundles 1.0.92-0); direct client transpilation passed instead.

Manual verification: open Settings, search `chat.agentSessions`, and read the descriptions for automatic marking as Done and permanent deletion. No behavior tests added or run because this is description-only.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup registers the chat configuration schema and localizes the two cleanup-setting descriptions.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Module evaluation creates two localized strings and registers the same two configuration properties as before; only shorter literal text and removal of unused interpolation arguments changed.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant work for exactly two configuration entries per module load; independent of session count, workspace size, or settings count beyond the unchanged registry behavior.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous one-time registration during module evaluation; no queue, fan-out, limiter, or additional asynchronous work introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Localization and configuration registry behavior are unchanged; the diff changes only literal values and removes formatting arguments, with no new cache keys, misses, or invalidation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: both changed hunks are confined to markdownDescription arguments and leave keys, defaults, agent-host mappings, migrations, and runtime consumers unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: String-localization cost is implementation-dependent but constant and slightly reduced; there is no plausible regression mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff neither adds eager heavyweight work nor increases startup allocations; the replacement descriptions are shorter.

Scenarios.Scenario: Users open or search Settings and render the descriptions for merged-session cleanup options.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The settings UI reads the already-registered markdownDescription and renders text. No cleanup operation, session enumeration, filesystem access, IPC, or network call is triggered by displaying the description.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most the same two setting rows for these keys; work scales only with description length, which decreases in the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Normal settings rendering remains unchanged; no new parallel or serialized operation is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No changed cache, lookup key, coalescing, or negative-cache behavior; only the displayed strings differ.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete diff and surrounding configuration schema: metadata only changed, while runtime setting identifiers and agent-host mappings remain identical.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact rendering cost is not measured, but the changed text is shorter and cannot establish increased CPU, memory, layout, or I/O cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Rendering frequency and cardinality are unchanged, and string size is reduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent-host lifecycle cleanup reads the two setting values and archives or deletes eligible merged sessions.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Lifecycle processing continues to read the unchanged agentHost keys and unchanged numeric values. The edited descriptions are not consumed on this runtime path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing lifecycle cleanup may remove eligible worktrees and session data based on the configured thresholds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing behavior scales with eligible merged sessions; effective cardinality is unchanged because setting IDs, defaults, and mapped agent-host keys are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same configuration values and agent-host keys controlled the same lifecycle cleanup operations before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations occur on the pre-existing lifecycle cleanup path, not while localizing or displaying the edited descriptions.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cleanup work may scale with session count, but the diff does not alter thresholds, defaults, scheduling, selection, or per-session operations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged lifecycle concurrency; no new task, loop, boundary fan-out, or scheduling behavior originates from the edited metadata.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration propagation behavior and keys are unchanged; no cache state is added or invalidated by the text edits.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: searches of both setting IDs and mapped agent-host keys show runtime consumers continue to depend on values and keys, not markdownDescription text.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The cost and prevalence of existing cleanup can vary with session history, but none of that work is introduced, moved, or amplified by this PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The only expensive transitive boundary is pre-existing and unreachable from the changed descriptive metadata.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete one-file, two-hunk diff and traced configuration registration, settings rendering, and agent-host lifecycle consumers. The PR only replaces two localized descriptions with shorter text and removes formatting arguments; it introduces no performance mechanism, boundary call, scaling work, retained state, or concurrency change.
